Question: A function \(f\) from the integers to the integers is defined as follows: \[ f(n)= \begin{cases} n+3 & \text{if \(n\) is odd},\\ \frac{n}{2} & \text{if \(n\) is even}. \end{cases} \] Suppose \(k\) is odd and \(f(f(f(k)))=27.\) What is the sum of the digits of \(k?\)
Solution:
An odd input becomes even when \(3\) is added. Since \(k\) is odd, its first two outputs are therefore
\[
f(k)=k+3,
\qquad
f(f(k))=\frac{k+3}{2}.
\]
Now consider the final output, \(27\). It cannot come from an odd input, because that branch always produces an even output. Its input must be even, and halving that input gives \(27\), so the input is \(54\).

Consequently,
\[
\frac{k+3}{2}=54,
\qquad
k=2\cdot54-3=105.
\]
This value is odd and satisfies the original condition:
\[
105\longrightarrow108\longrightarrow54\longrightarrow27.
\]
The sum of its digits is \(1+0+5=\boxed{6}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
